docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:1:# Life Consequence Reflow Law
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:13:No Step, path, schedule, or goal mutation can silently harm another active goal.
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:15:Ambitions may recommend reflow, but material consequences must be simulated, classified, and receipted before they affect the user's life system. The user should never discover later that a skipped Step, shrunken Step, source change, schedule install, or deadline adjustment quietly damaged another goal, broke protected time, erased proof value, or made a future deadline impossible.
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:17:Life Consequence Reflow is a Personal Life OS law. It is not analytics, scoring, shame, or a productivity dashboard. Its job is to protect the user's life system from hidden mutation.

docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:44:## Reflow Triggers
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:46:Every future runtime implementation that claims Life Consequence Reflow Green must evaluate these triggers:
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:52:| skip Step | Does skipping reduce proof value, break a dependency, delay a deadline, or increase recovery cost? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:53:| shrink Step | Does shrinking reduce proof, deadline protection, source validity, or downstream readiness? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:54:| extend Step | Does extending consume protected time, create density pressure, or cannibalize another active goal? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:55:| replace Step | Does replacement preserve source authority, proof, deadline, and dependency value? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:56:| split/merge Step | Does split/merge preserve traceability, receipts, and affected-goal visibility? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:58:| complete early | Does early completion open safe momentum, pull a next Step forward, or create overcommit risk? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:60:| source pack changes | Does new source tighten, loosen, revoke, or alter eligible paths and active Steps? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:61:| source revoked/stale | Does stale or revoked source block a current Step, schedule install, share path, or proof claim? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:62:| schedule availability changes | Does changed availability affect protected time, active deadlines, or installed Steps? |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:69:Life Consequence Reflow can be built in tiers, but Green claims must name the tier in scope:
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:73:| same-goal reflow | Reorders or adjusts Steps inside one goal. | Claiming cross-goal safety from same-goal proof only. |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:76:| treaty-aware reflow | Applies user-owned Goal Treaties before mutation. | Letting generic optimization override a treaty silently. |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:77:| source-change reflow | Re-evaluates affected paths and Steps when sources become fresh, stale, changed, contradicted, or revoked. | Letting stale/revoked source keep driving runtime behavior. |
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:111:## User Reflow Visibility Preferences
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:124:## Goal Treaty
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:126:A Goal Treaty is a user-owned constraint that declares how goals share life capacity.
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:135:Goal Treaties are not productivity rules, scores, or streaks. They are local, inspectable, user-owned agreements that future reflow must honor unless the user changes them. If a mutation would violate a treaty, the reflow must classify the consequence and require the appropriate visibility or block.
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:137:## Receipt Requirement
docs/codex/LIFE_CONSEQUENCE_REFLOW_LAW.md:147:Receipt content must be local-first and privacy-safe. A receipt is not optional when behavior changes. If source state changes caused the reflow, the receipt must also preserve source/freshness/revocation context or record why source authority is missing.

docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:1:# Step Elasticity Runtime Law
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:9:This law defines Step Elasticity as a non-optional runtime requirement for PLOS execution. It does not implement Elastic Step models, add UI controls, change generated Steps, alter Today, or claim Step Elasticity Engine behavior.
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:13:A Step is not a fixed task.
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:15:A Step is the current best expression of a goal path under the user's present time, energy, resources, source state, deadline, proof, and other active goals.
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:17:Step Elasticity is a runtime law, not a UI convenience. Ambitions must adapt Steps around real life without making the user fail a rigid app-authored task. Any shrink, extend, replace, split, merge, defer, proof-only, recovery-safe, or momentum-tail change must preserve inspectability, receipts, source authority, proof value, and cross-goal consequences.

docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:43:Every future runtime implementation that claims Step Elasticity Green must be able to reason about these forms:
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:48:| standard version | The default balanced expression for current time, energy, source state, and goal path. | Treating standard as the only true Step. |
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:58:| split version | A Step decomposed across time, proof, or dependency boundaries. | Splitting without preserving traceability and receipts. |
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:59:| merge version | Compatible Steps combined when it lowers overhead without losing meaning. | Merging unrelated goals or hiding consequence. |
docs/codex/STEP_ELASTICITY_RUNTIME_LAW.md:60:| replacement set | A set of alternatives when the current Step no longer fits. | Treating replacement as the only adaptation mode. |
